newsitem.title: UK: Report shows deep alcohol dependency in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Report shows deep alcohol dependency in Britain.

text.p: Twice as many Britons are dependent on alcohol as on all other drugs, resulting in violent crime, family breakup and millions of days of work lost, a report on Friday showed.
The report, Measures for Measures, published by the charity Alcohol Concern, said almost one in 20 Britons was dependent on alcohol compared with one in 45 on all other drugs.

"It's a thing that is embedded in our culture," said Eric Appleby, director of the London-based charity. "We have traditionally been a beer-drinking country." Though Britons rank middle in a world league of alcohol consumption, Appleby said the British "binge" culture was more damaging to health and led to more drink-related incidents.
"The binge-drinking culture is more prevalent in northern Europe than southern Europe. We don't have the cafe culture and one of the reasons for that is presumably the weather," he said.

The report showed that 44 percent of violent incidents in Britain were committed by drunk attackers. It said there were up to 33,000 alcohol-related deaths in Britain each year -- mainly from cancer, heart disease and cirrhosis -- while alcohol misuse cost British industry two billion pounds ($3.2 billion) a year.
Alcohol Concern urged the British government to introduce a National Alcohol Strategy to combat dependency.

The charity said it wanted the government to lower the drink-driving limit, educate children about the dangers of alcohol, develop services for people with drink problems and levy a tax on alcohol advertising.
In 1996, drinks companies spent 189 million pounds ($300 million) advertising their products in Britain, the report said.
But Appleby acknowledged the government might be reluctant to impose increased taxes on an industry that generates healthy revenues -- if not a healthy population.

He also said Alcohol Concern had a hard task to convince the public to cut down on drink. "It is an issue that people don't take seriously," he said. "Basically we enjoy it too much." ($1=.6271 Pound)
